title: Fix dequal Set/Map equality with repeated object members
prompt: This is a copy of the `dequal` deep-equality library (src/index.js). It reports some Sets and Maps as equal when they are not: for example a Set containing two equal-looking objects compares equal to a Set containing two different objects, and Maps with object keys have the same problem. Fix it so Set and Map comparison is correct, keeping the existing exports and the behavior for everything that is already right (order-insensitive Sets and Maps of objects must still compare equal).
answers: Yes, treat Set members and Map keys that are objects as needing a one-to-one match with the other side. Keep it dependency-free and keep the file plain ESM.
Sounds good. Please keep the fix small and do not change how arrays, dates, regexps or typed arrays compare.
That plan is fine, go ahead and make the change.

title: Add clsxUnique to clsx
prompt: This is a copy of the `clsx` class-name helper (src/index.js). Add a named export `clsxUnique(...args)` that accepts the same kinds of arguments as `clsx` (strings, numbers, arrays, objects, falsy values) but returns each whitespace-separated class token only once, in first-seen order, joined by single spaces. Tokens are case-sensitive. Leading, trailing and repeated whitespace are ignored, including inside object keys (an object key like "a b" contributes tokens "a" and "b"). `clsx` and the default export must behave exactly as before.
answers: Numbers count as tokens like in clsx, so 1 and "1" are the same token. Nothing else is special.
Yes, a single pass over a flattened token list is fine as long as clsx itself is untouched.
Looks good, go ahead.

title: Add literalRegExp helper to escape-string-regexp
prompt: This is a copy of `escape-string-regexp` (index.js). Add a named export `literalRegExp(string, options)` that returns a RegExp matching the given string literally. Options: `flags` (string, default none, passed to RegExp) and `wholeWord` (boolean, default false). With `wholeWord`, a match must not have a word character ([A-Za-z0-9_]) immediately before or after it, even if the string itself starts or ends with punctuation (so "c++" matches in "learn c++ now" but not in "c++x", and ".x" does not match in "a.x"). A non-string `string` throws TypeError; invalid flags throw whatever RegExp throws. It must work with the `u` flag. The default export must stay unchanged.
answers: Lookbehind/lookahead is fine, we only run on modern runtimes. Reuse the existing escape function rather than duplicating it.
Yes, `wholeWord` is only about the characters directly adjacent to the match, nothing about the string contents.
Plan looks right, go ahead.

title: Fix ms formatting that shows 60m instead of 1h
prompt: This is a JavaScript port of the `ms` duration library (src/ms.js). `format(3599999)` returns "60m" and `format(59500)` returns "60s" rather than rolling over to the next unit ("1h", "1m"). Fix `format` (short and long forms, positive and negative values) so a value that rounds up to the size of the next larger unit is shown in that unit, with pluralization following the unit actually shown (e.g. "1 hour"). Values that do not round up, sub-second values, `parse`, and the default export must stay as they are.
answers: Apply it to every unit boundary from seconds up to weeks. I do not care about rolling months into years.
Pluralization should follow the rule already in the code, evaluated for the unit that ends up displayed.
Fine, go ahead.

title: Refactor the ms CLI so its logic is testable
prompt: src/cli.js is a small command line wrapper around src/ms.js that reads process.argv, prints with console and calls process.exit directly, which makes it hard to test. Refactor it so the logic lives in an exported pure function `run(argv)` (argv excludes the node and script entries) returning `{code, stdout, stderr}` where stdout and stderr are the exact strings that would be printed, newline included. `run` must not touch console, process.argv or process.exit. `main()` and running the file as a script must behave exactly as they do now, apart from being built on `run`.
answers: Keep the existing messages and ordering exactly: usage text for no args goes to stderr with code 1, --help goes to stdout with code 0.
Yes, stdout and stderr are the concatenation of what was logged, one newline per line. main should just write them and exit with the code.
Good, go ahead.

title: Write a regression test suite for slash
prompt: index.js is the `slash` path helper (converts Windows backslash paths to forward slashes). There is no test suite yet. Write a thorough regression test suite in slash.test.js using `bun:test` that would catch realistic bugs introduced into index.js, covering its observable behavior and edge cases. Do not change index.js.

files.slash.test.js: // Tests for ./index.js go here. Run with `bun test`.

answers: Cover Windows drive paths, UNC paths, mixed separators and the extended-length prefix. Tests must pass against the current implementation.
Think about what a careless refactor of the replace or the prefix check could break and assert on those.
That works, go ahead.

title: Add compound durations across ms parse, format and CLI
prompt: This is a small copy of the `ms` duration library with a command line wrapper (src/ms.js, src/cli.js), a README, a test file, and review notes from the team in docs/REVIEW_NOTES.md. The team wants a compound duration style such as "1h 30m" supported end to end: when formatting numbers, when parsing strings, and in the CLI. Implement it as the review notes describe, keep everything that already works unchanged, and update the README and tests to match.

files.README.md:
# ms-lite (synthetic README)

A tiny duration helper derived from vercel/ms (MIT).

```js
import ms from './src/ms.js';
ms('2h');        // 7200000
ms(7200000);     // '2h'
ms(7200000, {long: true}); // '2 hours'
```

## CLI

```
ms [--long] <value>...
```

Numbers are formatted, strings are parsed.
files.docs/REVIEW_NOTES.md:
# Review notes: compound durations (synthetic)

Status: handoff from the last review round. Nobody on this list is available during implementation.
Items marked FALLBACK are the rule the team will use if the owner has not answered by merge time.

## Goal
Lots of dashboards want "1h 30m" instead of "2h" (the current output rounds). Add a "compound" style to
formatting, parsing and the CLI. The existing default style must keep working exactly as today.

## Priya (CLI owner)
- Flag is `--compound`, works together with `--long` in any order.
- `--help` and no-argument usage text must list the new flag: `Usage: ms [--long] [--compound] <value>...`
- Keep today's quirks: invalid values go to stderr as `Invalid duration: <arg>`, exit code 1, other values still print.
- A single quoted argument such as `"1h 30m"` must be parsed like any other value.

## Marcus (library reviewer)
- Wants all units down to seconds ("1d 1h 1m 1s"). Priya objects: unreadable on dashboards, two units is plenty.
- Months and years are not exact, so compound output never uses them (weeks is the largest unit).
  Parsing may still accept every unit that `parse` accepts today.
- Rounding makes "59m 59s" show as "1h", which is wrong for a countdown.
- OPEN, owner Dana (product): how many units, and truncate or round?
  FALLBACK: at most two adjacent units (for example h+m, d+h), remainder truncated toward zero, never rounded.
  If the second unit is zero it is left out ("1d" for 1d 5m). Under one second keep today's "ms" output.
  Pluralisation in long style follows the count of each unit shown ("1 hour 30 minutes").
  A negative value gets a single leading "-" on the first unit.

## Sam (parser owner)
- OPEN, owner Dana: should `parse` accept compound strings? Sam leans yes.
  FALLBACK: yes. Two or more terms separated by whitespace, each term is a non-negative number immediately
  followed by a unit ("1h 30m", "1.5h 30m"). A single leading "-" negates the whole value. Anything
  malformed is NaN, same as today (for example "1h 30", "1h30m", "1h -30m", leading or trailing spaces).
  Single-term input keeps its current behaviour, including "1 h" and "1.5 hours".

## Out of scope
- The default style shows "60m" for 3599999 ms. Known, tracked in a different ticket. Do not change default `format`.
- No new dependencies; keep plain ESM.

## Limits of this handoff
These notes are the only record of the team's views. They are not an approval of the final change.

answers: Compound output shows at most two adjacent units, truncating the remainder rather than rounding, with weeks as the largest unit. Anything under one second keeps today's ms output.

Yes, parse should accept compound strings like "1h 30m": two or more unit-suffixed terms separated by whitespace, with an optional single leading minus for the whole value. Anything malformed stays NaN.
That plan is fine: leave the default format and its rounding alone, add --compound to the CLI and its usage text, document it in the README, and go ahead.
